correctness.rationale: In the attached exact verifier, all 512 subsets of the 9-point Hesse configuration are enumerated by explicit line membership. The two complexes have 171 and 339 nonempty faces, and independently checked 504 and 1260 Hasse coverings. Iterated vertex toggling gives 79 and 163 disjoint ordinary face pairs; complete directed topological sorting proves each matching acyclic. Their critical cell vectors are (one 0-cell, one 2-cell, eleven 3-cells) and (one 0-cell, eleven 3-cells, one 4-cell). Unit integer Morse cancellation of every matched pair reduces the only possible signed boundaries, 1-by-11 and 11-by-1, to the exact zero matrices. Hurewicz in dimensions 2 and 3 proves the respective three- and four-cell attaching maps nullhomotopic, and therefore the claimed integral sphere wedges. Direct mod-two simplicial ranks independently corroborate the known Betti groups; finite enumeration is exhaustive in the claimed nine-vertex domain, not extrapolated.

originality.rationale: Lew 2021 Figure 1.1 already reports exactly the integral reduced homology of the same X_3: Z in dimension 2 and Z^11 in dimension 3. Alexander duality already determines homology of the theta complex, so neither homology calculation is new. The present single linked claim is the complete integral homotopy classification of both these specific complexes, proved via explicit acyclic matchings and zero attaching maps. Neither the inspected full relevant Lew section/chapter nor the two closely related published published-finding corpus full result texts states or implies this homotopy classification. value.rationale: The nine-point affine plane/Hesse 12-line configuration is the smallest nonbinary affine plane, a canonical finite incidence structure; Lew studies the line-free complex explicitly because of its rich integral homology. Its canonical theta Alexander dual is equally intrinsic. Existing homology and Alexander duality do not decide simple connectivity or whether higher cells attach nontrivially; the exact integral wedge homotopy classifications settle both for a natural complete object with explicit zero-attachment certificates. The two linked statements are one coherent dual determination, not isolated arbitrary numerical slices.
